source: Chopra et al. (2026) Thinking Ahead: Prospection-Guided Retrieval of Memory with Language Models
finding: Uses imagined future steps as retrieval probes (Simulate, Retrieve, Refine). Built on human prospection (Schacter, Addis, Hassabis). Memory facts far from the query in embedding space are found by asking what future steps will need.
numbers: MemoryQuest: 1,625 queries over 185 user profiles from 3 datasets. Recall 0.723 for PGR-TOT vs 0.256 for Mem0 and 0.160 for GraphRAG. RecallExact 0.326 vs 0.015 for Mem0. Query-only baseline recall 0.58.
quote: Inspired by prospection, the human ability to use imagined futures as cues for recall
limits: Generator GPT-4o. Gains partly because the benchmark was built with a low query-reference similarity filter (cosine <= 0.3), which favours the method. Extra LLM calls cost.
agent_relevance: Best direct use of a prospection mechanism in an agent loop: before retrieving, imagine what the next steps will need. Fits an S-state that plans ahead before recall.

source: Chopra et al. (2026) Thinking Ahead: Prospection-Guided Retrieval of Memory with Language Models
finding: Ablations on MemoryQuest: iterating the prospection (second round grounded by retrieved facts) helps; tree-of-thought barely beats linear chain.
numbers: Iterative: TOT recall 0.677 to 0.723, COT 0.645 to 0.718. TOT vs COT 0.723 vs 0.718 (win rate 55.67%). Adding prospection summary to answer: TOT 0.703 to 0.722, COT 0.722 to 0.735.
limits: Single benchmark ablation; small gaps between TOT and COT; no variance reported in the text I read.
agent_relevance: A cheap linear plan-ahead probe gets almost all of the gain; branching is not needed.

source: Chopra et al. (2026) Thinking Ahead: Prospection-Guided Retrieval of Memory with Language Models
finding: Preference judged by LLM judge and by blinded humans: prospection answers win against baselines. Result holds with a second generator.
numbers: Win rate 89-98% in pairwise LLM-judge comparisons; human annotation on held-out subsets 60-95%. DeepSeek-V3.2 as generator: MemoryQuest recall 0.748, RecallExact 0.348 (vs 0.723 / 0.326 with GPT-4o); ImplexConv 0.308 to 0.374; PersonaMem 0.210 to 0.229.
limits: LLM-judge preferences can favour longer, more personalised answers. Only two generator models.
agent_relevance: Gain is not model specific, so it is a scaffold effect, not a model quirk.

source: Mittal (2026) Did You Forget What I Asked? Prospective Memory Failures in Large Language Models
finding: Treats formatting-instruction compliance under a concurrent task as prospective memory (a deferred intention). Compliance falls when a demanding task runs at the same time.
numbers: 3 models (o4-mini, DeepSeek-V3.1, Llama-3.3-70B), over 8,000 prompts, tasks TriviaQA, MMLU, GSM8K, 5xGSM8K, CNN/DM. Compliance drops 2-21%. Mean drop: DeepSeek 10.2, o4-mini 8.9, Llama 6.0 points.
quote: a functional analog of prospective memory (PM)
limits: Load ordering is operational, not a validated cognitive scale. Analogy to human PM is functional only. Three runs per cell.
agent_relevance: Instructions given early are forgotten at the end of long work. Agent loop should re-state constraints at the end.

source: Mittal (2026) Did You Forget What I Asked? Prospective Memory Failures in Large Language Models
finding: Constraint type matters: terminal constraints (act at the end of the response) fail most; avoidance constraints are robust. Matches the human finding that delayed intentions need a cue at the right time.
numbers: Terminal constraints drop up to 50%; avoidance constraints nearly immune. Stacking: joint compliance falls as constraints accumulate.
limits: Taxonomy of five forgetting mechanisms from manual analysis of failures.
agent_relevance: Put end-of-output checks in the final verification state, not only at the prompt start.

source: Mittal (2026) Did You Forget What I Asked? Prospective Memory Failures in Large Language Models
finding: A salience-enhanced prompt (explicit framing plus trailing reminder) restores compliance. The cue works like an external reminder in human PM.
numbers: Restores 90-100% in many cells. At 5xGSM8K DeepSeek 100% (vs 72.2% natural), Llama 98.1% (vs 70.4%). Mean gain 17.7 (o4-mini), 16.9 (DeepSeek), 12.7 (Llama) points. Largest on CNN/DM (+13 to +21).
limits: Interference is two-way: with constraints, one model's GSM8K accuracy fell from 93% to 27%.
agent_relevance: Trailing reminder is nearly free and large. But do not stack many constraints.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) TriggerBench: Investigating Prospective Memory for Large Language Models
finding: Benchmark for latent-constraint recall without being asked (taxi-cello style). Pairs each scenario with a matched retrospective-memory control, negative variants (false alarms) and overloaded triggers.
numbers: Models: Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-235B Inst/Think, Gemma3-27B, GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-5.2; RAG; A-MEM, Mem0, Letta-sim. Five dimensions, daily and professional workflows.
quote: proactive recall, false-alarm rate, and attentional robustness under a single protocol
limits: PM Acc judged by GPT-4o at T=0, a possible bias. Scenarios are LLM-generated.
agent_relevance: Direct test of remembering to act later without a prompt. Good probe for our agent.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) TriggerBench: Investigating Prospective Memory for Large Language Models
finding: Test-time reasoning raises prospective recall, but pushes models to an always-remind habit.
numbers: Qwen3-235B-Think best open model PM Acc 74.86% (92.83% on Pos-Clean). GPT-5.2 +13.91 points from no thinking to high effort. GPT-5.2 high drops to 43.94% on negative controls; GPT-4o gets 82.7% on Neg-Clean but low recall.
limits: Precision-recall trade-off; positives-only scoring would mislead.
agent_relevance: Measure false alarms too; a planner that always warns is not prospecting.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) TriggerBench: Investigating Prospective Memory for Large Language Models
finding: Retrospective memory is intact while prospective memory collapses on the same context (the cognitive cliff).
numbers: GPT-4o RM accuracy about 98% up to 100K tokens; PM accuracy falls from over 90% to under 40%. Qwen3-235B-Think about 90% at 100K.
limits: Only some models run to 100K.
agent_relevance: Having the fact in context does not mean the agent will use it; need explicit trigger checks at action time.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) TriggerBench: Investigating Prospective Memory for Large Language Models
finding: PM as a probe of spare reasoning capacity: with an AIME problem between constraint and trigger, PM is higher when the math was solved.
numbers: 30-50K token band: AIME correct n=272 PM Acc 47.1%; AIME wrong n=143 PM Acc 37.8%.
limits: Correlational; 30 AIME-2025 problems.
agent_relevance: Low spare budget hurts remembering to check; leave reserve in states with heavy reasoning.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) TriggerBench: Investigating Prospective Memory for Large Language Models
finding: Standard RAG and memory systems (A-MEM, Mem0, Letta-sim) were also tested as ways to supply latent constraints at trigger time.
numbers: Retrieval used text-embedding-3-small, generation GPT-4.1. Specific scores not extracted by me.
limits: I read the setup, not the per-system numbers, so no figures given.
agent_relevance: Retrieval keyed on the trigger situation is the weak point; compare with PGR-style imagined-need probes.

source: ProMemAgent and CPMBench authors (2026) ProMemAgent: long-horizon proactive assistance with prospective memory
finding: Proactive agent that turns egocentric audio and video into prospective cues so a later event can trigger a deferred intention.
numbers: CPMBench: 1,000 instances, 8 everyday categories. Reported as strongest retrieval and best on long-horizon proactive assistance; no figures in abstract.
limits: Abstract only; numbers unseen.
agent_relevance: Linking prospective cues at write time is a design pattern we can copy.

source: Making Prospective Memory SLM-Shaped: Typed Intention Stores for Small-Model Agents (2026)
finding: Prospective Intention Store (PIS): a typed store of deferred intentions with lifecycle logic in code, not in the model. Small models match big-model scaffolds.
numbers: PM-Bench Set-F1: best published large-model scaffold 65.1%; DeepSeek-Chat+PIS 82.9%; Gemma-E2B 4.2% with no store, at most 6.6% with seven retrospective memories, 66.2% with PIS; PIS overall 70.1% vs retrospective at most 54.4%.
limits: Abstract only. Benchmark and method may share authors.
agent_relevance: Cheap scaffold: keep an explicit list of pending intentions with triggers and expiry, handled by code.

source: Bugaud (2026) CheeseBench: Evaluating LLMs on Rodent Behavioral Neuroscience Paradigms
finding: Nine rodent paradigms (Morris maze, radial arm maze, DNMS, etc.) as ASCII gridworlds, 13 LLMs, zero-shot with no task hints. No caching or future-planning paradigm included.
numbers: Rodent reference average 78.9%; random 38.0%; best open-weight (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) 68.0%; Claude Opus 4.7 86.7%; GPT-5.2-Codex and Opus 4.6 82.2%; Sonnet 4.6 81.1%.
quote: these results characterize the agent-plus-interface system, not the model in isolation
limits: Rodent baselines are approximate. Same model ranges 20% to 57% on interface settings alone.
agent_relevance: Shows comparative-cognition batteries can be run on LLM agents; closest published analogue to a scrub-jay style test. Treat as design template.

source: Bugaud (2026) CheeseBench
finding: Working memory across choices (radial arm maze) is the hard paradigm for open models; frontier models solve it.
numbers: Radial arm maze: open-weight 0-10%, Qwen2.5-VL-7B 0% vs rodents 70%; Claude Opus 4.7 100%, Opus 4.6 90%, GPT-4.1 0% (action bias, about 3x calls). Operant conditioning 98%; spatial 57%; shuttle avoidance 70%.
limits: Few trials per environment (12-100). Per-seed variance not read.
agent_relevance: Within-episode state tracking, needed for planning ahead, differs sharply across models.

source: Bugaud (2026) CheeseBench
finding: Scaffold effects: shorter history is better and chain-of-thought hurts.
numbers: Qwen2.5-VL-7B ablation: default prompt 46.7%, CoT 31.9%, minimal 35.6%, few-shot 29.6%. History h=5 about 57%. Authors say effect sizes approximate.
limits: Ablation on one 7B model with fixed seeds; CoT verbose output displaces observation history.
agent_relevance: Do not assume more reasoning text helps embodied-style loops; cap context and keep a short free-text working-memory note (500 chars).

source: Position: Episodic Memory is the Missing Piece for Long-Term LLM Agents (2025)
finding: Argues LLM agents need episodic memory with five properties: long-term storage, explicit reasoning, single-shot learning, instance-specific and contextualized memories. Compares RAG, GraphRAG, fine-tuning and state-space models in a table.
numbers: No experiments. Properties read from PDF text extraction.
limits: Position paper only; no measured results. Frames future use as an agent need, not a test of mental time travel.
agent_relevance: Background framing: our agent needs episodic traces that can be recombined for planning.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
finding: Agent loop with observation, reflection and daily planning stored in language. Planning ahead and re-planning are an older AI use of prospection.
numbers: 25 agents, a Valentine's Day party spread over two days; ablation says each of observation, planning, reflection contributes to believability (abstract only; numbers not read by me).
limits: I could only open the abstract page; full ablation numbers not verified.
agent_relevance: Plan-then-revise loop is already a mental time travel analogue in agents.

source: Pataranutaporn et al. (2024) Future You: A Conversation with an AI-Generated Future Self
finding: LLM builds a synthetic future memory and chats as the user at age 60. Preregistered between-subjects trial; strengthens future self-continuity and lowers anxiety.
numbers: N=344 analysed of 400. Groups: Future You 73, questionnaire 76, generic chat 103, control 92. Anxiety change: -0.68 vs +0.21 control (F(3,376)=5.13, p=0.002). FSC change +0.42 vs 0.00 control (Welch F=8.57, p<0.001). My rough d about -0.67 (anxiety), 0.76 (FSC); not reported by authors.
limits: Single session, ages 18-30, GPT-3.5, self-report outcomes, no long-term follow-up. Future You vs generic chat on anxiety p=0.059.
agent_relevance: LLM can be a prospection scaffold for a human, not just a user of prospection; little for our solo agent.

source: Future You: Designing and Evaluating Multimodal AI-generated Digital Twins (2025)
finding: Randomized trial of text, voice and avatar future selves versus neutral control. All raised future self-continuity, wellbeing, motivation.
numbers: N=92. Formats did not differ significantly. Claude 4 beat ChatGPT 3.5, Llama 4, Qwen 3 on outcomes.
limits: Abstract only; small N; model comparison details not seen.
agent_relevance: Model choice mattered for generating a convincing future self.

source: AI-Facilitated Episodic Future Thinking For Adults with Obesity (2025)
finding: EFTeacher chatbot (GPT-4-Turbo) writes episodic future thinking cues, a method from the delay-discounting literature.
numbers: Mixed-methods usability study; no outcome statistics in abstract. Users liked personalisation; some found it repetitive and verbose.
limits: Feasibility only, no delay discounting measured.
agent_relevance: Shows the human EFT method now run by LLMs; no evidence it changes LLM behaviour.

source: Delay-of-Gratification as a Multi-Agent Survival Micro-benchmark for Long-Horizon LLMs (2026)
finding: Marshmallow-test style benchmark for ReAct agents, minute by minute, with the option to ask a question via a tool.
numbers: 19,200 trajectories, 64 cells. 75.9% persist to the end. About 7.12 questions per agent; budget hit in 6% of minutes. Broadcast (social) raises early eating risk vs isolation; mandatory self-questioning raises risk. Removing hedonic drive and age persona gives completion near 1.0.
limits: Abstract only; models not named; persona prompts do most of the work, so it measures role-play, not true delay discounting.
agent_relevance: Suggests forcing self-reflection can hurt persistence; keep it optional.

source: Efficient Agentic Reasoning Through Self-Regulated Simulative Planning (SR2AM, 2026)
finding: Agent learns when and how far ahead to simulate future states with the LLM as world model; RL extends horizon more than frequency.
numbers: v1.0-30B uses 25.8-95.3% fewer reasoning tokens; RL raises average planning horizon 22.8% but frequency only 2.0%. v0.1-8B competitive with 120-355B systems.
limits: Abstract only; task suite math, science, tabular, web.
agent_relevance: Matches foresight use: plan further, not more often; a learned gate on when to simulate.

source: Search coverage note (this run, 2026-11-17)
finding: Several arXiv keyword searches (episodic future thinking, mental time travel, future needs and animal cognition, delay discounting) found no LLM replication of the scrub jay (Raby 2007) or Bischof-Koehler meal-planning paradigm. Only CheeseBench (rodent paradigms) and delayed-reward agent tasks came close.
numbers: Zero direct LLM tests of the caching or future-need paradigm in about 12 searches. Not exhaustive: search budget and API limits blocked WebSearch, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar.
limits: Absence of evidence in a limited search only.
agent_relevance: Do not claim an LLM scrub jay result; this is an open gap.

source: Mittal (2026) PM paper, model list and human PM references
finding: Paper cites Einstein and McDaniel (2005) and McDaniel (2000) on human PM, and frames cue salience as the human-like fix.
numbers: Models o4-mini, DeepSeek-V3.1 (open-weight, Azure AI), Llama-3.3-70B; 95% CIs from 3 runs.
limits: Three runs per condition only; one family each.
agent_relevance: Human PM theory (cue focality) gives a testable lever for agents.
